title: RPyYARV, Runtime-Preserving Variant: A Meta-Tracing YARV Interpreter on CRuby's Heap (snapshot 2026.10)
abstract: This is a source snapshot of RPyYARV, the runtime-preserving variant. RPyYARV is an interpreter for YARV, CRuby's bytecode, written in RPython. A meta-tracing JIT compiler is generated from this interpreter. The interpreter runs inside CRuby itself. It uses CRuby's own heap, object layout and garbage collector, next to the RPython runtime's collector. This is how it preserves the runtime.This variant takes a conservative approach. RPyYARV pins every CRuby object it holds, so CRuby's collector never moves an object that compiled code still refers to. The snapshot is the code evaluated in the preprint "Keep the Runtime, Derive the JIT Compiler: Runtime-Preserving Meta-Tracing with Two Coexisting Garbage Collectors" (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23288661). Over 85 benchmarks of ruby-bench, it takes 0.37 of CRuby's interpreter time. Against YJIT it takes 0.97 of YJIT's time (95% confidence interval 0.83 to 1.14), which is on par.A separate object-copying variant also exists. It copies the object model into the RPython VM. That variant is not part of this snapshot.

title: Federated Spiking GANs with Rényi Differential Privacy for privacy-preserving synthetic EEG generation in brain–computer interfaces
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) data used in brain-computer and brain-machine interfaces (BCI/BMI) contain sensitive, user-specific information, creating privacy risks in consumer applications such as gaming, human augmentation, and virtual reality. Existing methods like encryption and anonymization either fail to protect data during analysis or still expose identifiable attributes. While differential privacy (DP) offers formal protection, it often reduces data utility. The key challenge is to generate synthetic EEG data that protects sensitive attributes while retaining temporal features for downstream use. To address this, we developed a federated spiking generative framework that integrates a spiking neural network (SNN)-based generator, temporally correlated noise, an artificial neural network (ANN)-based discriminator, and Rényi differential privacy (RDP) within a federated learning framework. The SNN-based generator captures temporal characteristics, and the ANN-based discriminator maintains classification accuracy. Federated training prevents centralization of raw client data, while privacy is preserved through controlled perturbation of spike-train and membrane-potential representations, supported by RDP-based privacy accounting. We evaluated our architecture against methods such as RDP-TimeGAN, RDP-CRNN-GAN, RDP-RCGAN, and RDP-Clare-GAN, demonstrating that our approach preserves temporal features and downstream utility while maintaining privacy in synthetic EEG generation. This solution enables privacy-preserving generation of distributed synthetic EEG data for BCI/BMI research and development.

title: jekylldown: Create, Build and Serve 'Jekyll' Websites from 'R Markdown' and 'Quarto'
abstract: Create, Build and Serve 'Jekyll' Websites from 'R Markdown' and 'Quarto' Version 0.3.4Description Do for 'Jekyll' what 'blogdown' does for 'Hugo': create sites from the most popular themes ('al-folio', 'Chirpy', 'Minimal Mistakes', 'minima'), write posts in R Markdown or 'Quarto' that are knitted to Markdown consumed natively by 'Jekyll', customize theme colors, fonts and elements declaratively from R, migrate 'blogdown'/'Hugo' sites, build and serve the site locally with live reload, and diagnose the Ruby/'Jekyll' toolchain.'Jekyll' is invoked strictly via its command line interface; no R-Ruby language bridge is used.

title: RIDI-REAL-UPDATES-v1: Prospective locked protocol for individual correctness changes across released AI model updates
abstract: This is the complete, prospective execution-lock registration for RIDI-REAL-UPDATES-v1. It is a separate public registration linked to the incomplete earlier narrative record https://osf.io/pkde5/ and the related, distinct RIDI-PREDICT record https://osf.io/xrzp5/. At submission, scientific model-generation units completed: 0/24. This is not a report of outcomes or an attempt to repair P8; P8 remains INCOMPLETE. Study design: Six pinned incumbent-to-successor language-model pairs (12 exact revisions), applied to 800 frozen reference questions drawn from Natural Questions (250), HotpotQA (250), and FEVER (300), with original BM25 retrieved top-10 contexts. Each model runs a single-question main condition and a 16-question replay-floor condition. The preregistered endpoints compare aggregate accuracy, paired individual-question correctness changes, replay noise and whether frozen RIDI-PREDICT fragility F_B predicts those changes. Confirmatory thresholds and 100,000 within-benchmark paired bootstrap resamples are specified in the archived protocol. The accompanying five public files include exact LOCK.json, the full prospective protocol, executable code and environment records in a ZIP, public hashes/provenance (including SHA-256 of private study inputs), and a transparent correction notice for pkde5. The scientific lock includes SHA-256 hashes of 30 files and has SHA-256 3863feda6293287b744a79de13bf5571411473422fb319521a021de37ebd17c0. Restricted input passages, gold answers and prior outputs are not redistributed in the public archive. Verified GPU/storage preflight was preparatory only; there are no new study answers yet. Important disclosures: The initial record pkde5 was registered before this complete execution lock and did not contain the intended archived supporting files. It must not be described as having frozen the present protocol. Prior RIDI-PREDICT transfer analyses, the post-run recovery in that earlier study, and some Qwen3 reference results were known to the author; Qwen3-8B is not an entirely unseen target of the fragility predictor. 'Accepted' means a preregistered study scoring rule, not an actual provider deployment authorization.

title: Perfect and peak state transfer on IBM quantum hardware
abstract: We run continuous-time quantum walks with perfect and peak state transfer on a present-day superconducting quantum processor, IBM Quantum's $156$-qubit Heron device ibm_kingston, deliberately without error correction or error mitigation. Perfect state transfer and its relaxations have been studied extensively in algebraic graph theory, where one can prove exactly which graphs move a quantum state from one vertex to another with probability one (or with the largest probability the graph allows, in the case of peak state transfer), and at what time. Our experiments cover perfect state transfer on the hypercubes $Q_2 = C_4$ and $Q_3$, and on the Hamming-weighted paths $\mathrm{HP}_n$, the equitable-partition quotients of the hypercubes $Q_n$, for $n$ up to $20$; peak state transfer on the $X_n$ family for $n$ up to $11$; and, for comparison, moving the state along a path of qubits by a sequence of SWAP gates.

title: Analog RF Computing for Integrated Data and AI Flows Over Wireless Networks
abstract: Many resource-constrained edge devices require artificial intelligence (AI) services but are not powerful enough to store or execute neural networks (NNs). Analog radio frequency (RF) computing addresses this limitation by letting a base station (BS) multicast a waveform encoding NN weights to different clients. Each client then multiplies the received weight-encoded waveform with its locally generated input-encoded waveform through a passive mixer in its RF frontend, thereby realizing the matrix-vector multiplications (MVMs) needed for AI inference with an extremely low power and memory requirement. This can enable telecom operators to provide AI inference services to the edge devices connected to their networks. In practice, however, this multicast AI flow must share the spectrum, power, and spatial resources with other data flows. This paper considers a multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-MIMO) downlink scenario and studies the resulting relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating the multicast AI flow with the unicast data flows. We formulate a joint beamforming problem for the data and AI flows to maximize the aggregate data rate subject to computing accuracy, client energy, total power, and hardware-related constraints. We develop a weighted minimum mean-square error (WMMSE)-based algorithm to solve the problem. Numerical results based on 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) channels show that the relative aggregate data rate reduction from integrating an AI flow with data flows is below 5% in representative settings. This indicates that telecom operators can use analog RF computing to provide edge AI services while providing data communication services simultaneously.

title: Learning Topology-Aware Representations for Mechanics-Relevant TPMS Metamaterials
abstract: Learning informative representations of mechanical Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) metamaterials is important for mechanics analysis and structural design, yet existing methods have rarely explicitly supervised learned representations with information about global structural connectivity that is relevant to mechanical response. We propose a topology-aware representation learning framework that integrates persistent homology into a DMAE backbone to explicitly encode global structural connectivity. A persistence-guided masking strategy prioritizes patches associated with persistent topological features, while an auxiliary persistent-homology decoder encourages the latent representation to retain information about topological feature counts across connected components, tunnels, and voids. We evaluate the learned representations on two complementary TPMS datasets using family classification, mechanical-property classification, unsupervised clustering, and regression. Across the two datasets, our method demonstrates strong performance in both structural family and mechanical-property classification, improving family classification by up to 3.9% while achieving the best linear-probe performance. More notably, unsupervised property-clustering performance improves by up to 26.7% and 51.5% across the two datasets, while strong regression performance is retained with $R^2=0.993$. These results establish persistent topology as an effective inductive bias for representation learning of complex three-dimensional mechanical metamaterials.

title: Intermediate memory costs of quantum channel synthesis with a protected subsystem
abstract: A quantum memory can preserve a subsystem perfectly while discarding information needed by a later operation. We study the total intermediate dimension required for channel synthesis when the first stage protects a $b$-dimensional subsystem and has a prescribed noncommutative graph imposing full confusability on an $a$-dimensional control register. For a finite family of classically controlled branches, exact synthesis is possible if and only if the target graph contains the prescribed graph of the first stage. For every feasible family, we construct a single processor that implements all branches exactly. The processor uses pairwise nonorthogonal pure program states in a register of dimension at most $a$. A target graph may be realizable with a carrier of dimension $b$, while synthesizing a channel with that graph can require dimension $ab$. We also characterize the closure of the attainable channels, distinguishing exact synthesis from arbitrarily accurate approximation. Finally, for a family built from the trine communication task, a four-dimensional carrier permits exact synthesis with quantum programs under output depolarization. At the same total carrier dimension and without free shared randomness, classical programs have optimal normalized diamond error $(1-η)/4$, where $0\leqη\leq1$ is the depolarization strength. For $η<1$, the gap persists under sufficiently small perturbations of the target branches.

title: Drivers of LLM Consensus Formation Under Competing Incentives: A Simulation Study
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent environments that produce unanimous agreement, both in intended interactions that need coordination and in unintended emergent interactions. Consequently, understanding how LLMs with competing incentives reach consensus is crucial to better interpret and design LLM collectives. We introduce an evaluation, based on the Network Consensus game, to assess the mechanisms driving this process. Here, a network of agents must agree on one of two colours to receive a payoff, but agents are offered different payoffs for the agreed colour. We vary components such as communication access and network structure and assess six open-source models and one closed model (ChatGPT 5.6-sol). We find that open-source LLMs reach consensus less often than humans in comparable experiments and only if messages are communicated across the global network. ChatGPT 5.6-sol, however, is able to reach consensus with communication limited to its neighbours and with no communication ability. This is achieved through lower stubbornness and higher majority-following tendencies, and by providing more information about its neighbours' states in messages. However, situating agents in a highly clustered graph reduces consensus, regardless of these traits, demonstrating that both system design and individual model traits drive collective outcomes.

title: Recursive Gradient Retraction Methods for Stochastic Nonconvex Optimization on Stiefel Manifolds
abstract: Nonconvex optimization on Stiefel manifolds underlies many problems in machine learning and deep learning. However, existing stochastic Riemannian retraction methods often rely on stepsizes that require prior knowledge of the gradient Lipschitz constant, a prescribed iteration horizon, or restrictive batch-size choices. We develop {\sf RGR}, a recursive gradient retraction method for stochastic nonconvex optimization on Stiefel manifolds. Instead of recursively updating gradient estimators in changing tangent spaces, {\sf RGR} constructs them in the Euclidean space and subsequently maps them to tangent space, thereby avoiding vector transport. The method comprises three variants: {\sf RGR-SPIDER} for finite-sum optimization and {\sf RGR-SRM} and {\sf RGR-EMA} for online stochastic optimization. {\sf RGR-SPIDER} is Lipschitz-free and horizon-free, as its adaptive stepsize requires neither prior knowledge of the gradient Lipschitz constant nor a prescribed iteration horizon. {\sf RGR-SRM} and {\sf RGR-EMA} are mini-batch and horizon-free methods whose convergence guarantees do not rely on prescribed large batch sizes and whose parameters can be chosen without prior knowledge of the total iteration budget. We show that {\sf RGR-SPIDER} reaches an $\varepsilon$-critical point using $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-2})$ iterations and $\mathcal{O}(N+\sqrt{N}\varepsilon^{-2})$ component-gradient evaluations, where $N$ denotes the number of component functions. For the online setting, {\sf RGR-SRM} and {\sf RGR-EMA} achieve iteration complexities of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\varepsilon^{-3})$ and $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\varepsilon^{-4})$, respectively. Experiments on principal component analysis, low-rank matrix completion, and orthogonal convolutional neural networks demonstrate faster empirical convergence than methods that construct recursive gradient estimators directly in Riemannian tangent spaces.

title: APPLICATION OF DEEP REINFORCEMENT LEARNING FOR CONTROL OF SERVICE ROBOT MANIPULATORS IN UNSTRUC-TURED ENVIRONMENTS
abstract: This paper examines the control of robotic manipulators in unstructured environ-ments using deep reinforcement learning. The limitations of classical approaches are substantiated, and a hybrid architecture combining DRL and impedance control for safe contact is proposed. The challenges of sim-to-real policy transfer are analyzed, and recommendations for algorithm selection are provided, taking into account the computational resources of onboard systems.

title: Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning for Cooperative Control of Multiple Unmanned Surface Vehicle in Neutralizing Threat Vessels
abstract: This study proposes a cooperative capture system in which two allied unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) jointly deploy a capture net to intercept noncooperative vessels in naval environments. To overcome the limitations of traditional rule-based methods subjected to environmental uncertainties, a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework is developed within a high-fidelity, unity-based simulation environment incorporating the Gerstner wave and wind disturbance models. Each agent utilizes an egocentric polar coordinate observation space; distance values are normalized via a nonlinear rational function to prioritize close-range sensitivity, while angular discontinuities are resolved through trigonometric transformations. The Multi-Agent POsthumous Credit Assignment algorithm is adopted within a Centralized Training with Decentralized Execution architecture, enabling robust strategy learning through posthumous credit assignment even when agents exit the environment. The reward structure is designed hierarchically, combining sparse event rewards for capture success with dense continuous rewards based on formation maintenance, target approach, and heading alignment. Quantitative experimental results demonstrate that the proposed MARL-based approach significantly outperforms the modified Line-of-Sight guidance law, achieving a 65% capture success rate and a three-fold reduction in formation collapse under dynamic sea conditions. This study confirms that the proposed framework effectively enables autonomous USVs to learn complex, coordinated maneuvers for physical maritime interdiction, providing a robust solution for securing maritime security.

title: Adaptive Self–Mutual Mechanism Switching in Parallel-World and Multi-LLM Systems: A Unified Framework for Autonomous and Collaborative Intelligence
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can solve problems through autonomous processing, including self-reflection, self-diagnosis, self-correction, self-verification, self-planning, and self-evaluation. They can also collaborate through mutual reflection, cross-model diagnosis, collaborative correction, cross-verification, collaborative planning, and mutual evaluation. However, a system that consistently relies on autonomous processing may preserve its own reasoning errors, whereas a system that consistently activates multiple models may incur unnecessary computational costs, propagate correlated errors, or become vulnerable to unproductive interactions. This paper proposes Adaptive Self–Mutual Mechanism Switching in Parallel-World and Multi-LLM Systems (ASMS-PW), a unified framework that dynamically selects between autonomous and collaborative mechanisms according to task characteristics, uncertainty, historical reliability, disagreement, expected improvement, and computational cost. The framework introduces parallel worlds, defined as multiple independently configured processing instances derived from the same underlying LLM, which can adopt different reasoning objectives, procedural strategies, evaluation criteria, or information-processing directions. These parallel worlds can interact with one another and with heterogeneous external LLMs. Rather than restricting the system to a single predefined self–mutual mechanism pair, ASMS-PW treats mechanism selection as a sequential decision problem. A controller estimates the expected utility of available actions, including autonomous processing, parallel-world interaction, heterogeneous multi-model collaboration, and external verification. It then selects, combines, or switches mechanisms as the task evolves, subject to a computational budget and task-specific constraints. This paper formalizes the framework, defines its architectural components and switching policy, presents an operational algorithm, and proposes an empirical evaluation protocol. The central research questions concern whether adaptive switching improves task performance, reliability, computational efficiency, and robustness compared with static autonomous processing, static collaboration, and existing adaptive collaboration methods. The framework is intended to provide a generalizable basis for investigating self–mutual mechanisms across reasoning, learning, planning, diagnosis, verification, memory, reward estimation, and model coordination. Its effectiveness and novelty as a complete implementation remain to be established through systematic experiments and further literature comparison.

title: Adaptive Switching Between Individual Adaptive Learning and Collaborative Adaptive Learning for Multiple Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) possess different capabilities, limitations, adaptation requirements, and computational costs. Although individual adaptation enables each model to improve its performance independently, collaborative adaptation allows multiple models to exchange feedback, compare solutions, identify complementary knowledge, and coordinate their learning processes. Relying exclusively on either mode may limit learning efficiency, particularly when task difficulty, uncertainty, model competence, and resource availability change over time. This paper proposes Adaptive Switching between Individual Adaptive Learning and Collaborative Adaptive Learning (AS-ICL), a conceptual framework that dynamically selects between independent model adaptation and cross-model collaborative adaptation according to observed learning conditions. Unlike a fixed learning strategy, AS-ICL incorporates a switching controller that evaluates performance trends, uncertainty, disagreement, learning progress, expected collaboration benefits, and computational costs. The controller selects individual adaptation when independent learning is sufficiently effective and switches to collaborative adaptation when cross-model interaction is expected to provide additional value. Feedback from both modes is recorded to improve subsequent switching decisions. The framework comprises individual learning agents, a collaboration mechanism, a state-monitoring module, an adaptive switching controller, a shared experience interface, and a feedback-based policy optimizer. A mathematical formulation, algorithmic procedure, experimental hypotheses, and evaluation protocol are presented. The proposed framework is intended to support more flexible learning strategies while avoiding unnecessary collaboration, repetitive reasoning, and excessive communication costs. Because this paper introduces a conceptual framework rather than reporting completed experiments, its effectiveness remains an empirical research question.

title: TECA: Temporal Evolution with Convolutional Block Attention for Knowledge Graph Reasoning
abstract: Temporal Knowledge Graph (TKG) reasoning aims to infer time-dependent facts by modeling how entities and relations evolve. Most existing methods learn entity and relation embeddings jointly from past observations and often treat relations as auxiliary signals induced by entity interactions. This coupling can over-smooth relation representations and weaken the model’s ability to capture relation-specific semantics, logical dependencies, and context shifts that are crucial for predicting future facts. To overcome this limitation, we propose TECA (Temporal Evolution with Convolutional Block Attention), a relation-centric module designed to explicitly model relation evolution in temporal graphs. TECA builds time-aware relation representations by integrating static semantics with temporal dynamics, and employs a lightweight Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) that combines channel attention and spatial attention. Channel attention adaptively reweights semantic feature dimensions, while spatial attention highlights informative local interactions, enabling the model to emphasize the most discriminative relational cues under changing temporal contexts. We evaluate TECA on four widely used TKG benchmarks (ICEWS14, ICEWS18, ICEWS05–15, and GDELT) covering different temporal granularities and relational complexities. Extensive experiments and component analyses show that TECA consistently surpasses recent state-of-the-art baselines, achieving improvements of up to 6.1 MRR points and 6.3 Hits@10 points. The results indicate that explicitly enhancing relation evolution is a key factor for robust and accurate TKG reasoning.

title: Chatbots no atendimento acadêmico em uma instituição do SENAC: desenvolvimento e avaliação de uma assistente virtual
abstract: Este artigo tem como objetivo apresentar o desenvolvimento e a avaliação da ANE, uma assistente virtual baseada em chatbot, desenvolvida para apoiar o atendimento acadêmico na Faculdade Senac Goiás. O estudo caracteriza-se como uma pesquisa aplicada, de abordagem quali-quantitativa, conduzida no primeiro semestre de 2025, a partir da análise de demandas reais da Secretaria Acadêmica e da implementação da solução por meio da plataforma Dialogflow, ferramenta da Google voltada ao processamento de linguagem natural. A solução foi projetada para responder dúvidas relacionadas a vestibular, processos administrativos e informações gerais dos cursos. A avaliação foi realizada com 15 participantes, incluindo estudantes, docentes, técnicos administrativos e membros da comunidade externa, por meio de um questionário estruturado em dimensões relacionadas à clareza das respostas, facilidade de uso, utilidade da informação, satisfação com a interação e impacto na experiência acadêmica. Os dados foram analisados por estatística descritiva e pela análise interpretativa das respostas abertas. Os resultados indicaram predominância de avaliações positivas nas dimensões analisadas, especialmente quanto à compreensão das respostas, à utilidade das informações e à percepção de economia de tempo. Conclui-se que a adoção de chatbots no atendimento acadêmico pode contribuir para ampliar o acesso à informação, padronizar respostas institucionais e apoiar a experiência dos usuários em serviços educacionais.

A avaliação foi realizada com 15 participantes, incluindo estudantes, docentes, técnicos administrativos e membros da comunidade externa, por meio de um questionário estruturado em dimensões relacionadas à clareza das respostas, facilidade de uso, utilidade da informação, satisfação com a interação e impacto na experiência acadêmica. Os dados foram analisados por estatística descritiva e pela análise interpretativa das respostas abertas. Os resultados indicaram predominância de avaliações positivas nas dimensões analisadas, especialmente quanto à compreensão das respostas, à utilidade das informações e à percepção de economia de tempo. Conclui-se que a adoção de chatbots no atendimento acadêmico pode contribuir para ampliar o acesso à informação, padronizar respostas institucionais e apoiar a experiência dos usuários em serviços educacionais.

title: DeepPV-MRF: End-to-End Partial-Volume Fraction Estimation from MR Fingerprinting Time Series
abstract: Background: Estimating subvoxel tissue fractions from magnetic resonance fingerprinting (MRF) is challenging. Conventional dictionary matching and segmentation pipelines can propagate errors from intermediate parametric maps into tissue fraction estimates. Purpose: We introduce DeepPV-MRF, a deep learning framework that directly estimates voxel-wise tissue fractions from raw MRF signals. Methods: A cascaded spatial-temporal network was trained on subject-derived Bloch simulations with radial k-space undersampling. The network combines temporal encoding and spatial U-Net refinement to estimate cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), gray matter (GM), and white matter (WM) fractions without intermediate T1/T2 maps. We compared DeepPV-MRF with partial-volume dictionary matching (PV-DM) and pseudoinverse estimation (PV-Pinv) using simulated and in vivo data. Results: DeepPV-MRF outperformed both methods across acquisition settings. In single-shot simulations, CSF/WM/GM mean absolute errors were 0.0418/0.0744/0.0757, versus 0.1281/0.2443/0.2958 for PV-DM and 0.2021/0.2793/0.2630 for PV-Pinv. Corresponding structural similarity values were 0.960/0.916/0.922. In vivo results showed sharper anatomical boundaries and smoother tissue transitions, while cross-shot analysis indicated improved consistency across volunteers. Conclusions: DeepPV-MRF enables accurate and efficient direct tissue fraction estimation from MRF signals, particularly with limited shots. Further validation is needed before clinical deployment.

title: DeBoneDiT: Depth-Driven Conditional Bridge Diffusion Transformers for Bone Suppression in Chest X-Ray Images
abstract: Chest X-Ray (CXR) is a primary modality for diagnosing pulmonary diseases, yet the overlap of bony structures often obscures critical radiographic findings, increasing the risk of diagnostic uncertainty. While Dual-Energy Subtraction (DES) is the clinical benchmark for bone suppression, its widespread adoption is primarily hindered by specialized hardware requirements and increased radiation exposure. Recently, diffusion-based generative models have shown promise for this task, yet they are still constrained by reconstruction-biased latent compression, prior-induced domain gap, and a scarcity of high-quality paired datasets. To address these challenges, we propose DeBoneDiT, a depth-driven conditional bridge diffusion Transformer architecture for efficient high-resolution bone suppression. We first introduce Depth Auto-Encoder (DAE), a structure-aware vision tokenizer for latent compression. By incorporating a multi-level depth feature loss derived from the pretrained Depth Anything V2 encoder, DAE preserves both visual fidelity and structural consistency. Second, we formulate bone suppression as a source-conditioned Brownian bridge diffusion process, leveraging CXRs as both the diffusion prior and structural guidance to narrow the source-to-target domain gap and maintain anatomical plausibility. Furthermore, we have constructed and released SZCH-X-Rays, the largest publicly available high-quality paired dataset for bone suppression to date, comprising 741 pairs of CXR and DES soft tissue images. Extensive experiments and downstream evaluation demonstrate that DeBoneDiT achieves superior bone suppression performance with reduced computational overhead.

title: Supplementary data and analysis materials for “Curvature-Based Shrinkage for Label-Budgeted Recalibration under Dataset Shift: An Empirical Risk Study”
abstract: This item contains supplementary data and analysis materials supporting the manuscript “Curvature-Based Shrinkage for Label-Budgeted Recalibration under Dataset Shift: An Empirical Risk Study” by Jufeng Li and Wenjie Li.Online_Resource_1.pdf provides conditional theoretical derivations, complete corrected result tables, domain eligibility criteria, statistical analysis details, and sensitivity analyses.Online_Resource_2.zip contains archived evaluation metrics, domain and protocol metadata, corrected analysis tables, statistical reanalysis code, and excerpts of the calibration implementation. The accompanying README explains the file structure, dependencies, analysis procedure, and limitations.The study examines curvature-based shrinkage and gated temperature recalibration under limited target-label budgets. The archived evaluation covers remote-sensing sampling differences, population differences in activity recognition, and calendar-based shifts in restaurant inspections. Results distinguish the frequency of harmful recalibration from its severity.The statistical reanalysis uses existing archived outcomes without retraining classifiers or changing fitted temperatures. The package supports reproduction of the reported statistical summaries; it is not a complete standalone environment for retraining all models. Repeating model training requires the original datasets and the corresponding training environment.The authors received no financial support for this research.

title: Fanlarini intellektual adaptiv ta'lim texnologiyalari asosida o'qitish
abstract: Mazkur tezisda oliy ta'lim muassasalarida amaliy matematika fanlarini o'qitish jarayonida intellektual adaptiv ta'lim texnologiyalaridan foydalanish imkoniyatlari yoritilgan. Zamonaviy ta'lim jarayonida talabalarning bilim darajasi, o'zlashtirish sur'ati va individual ta'lim ehtiyojlari bir-biridan farq qilishi sababli barcha talabalar uchun yagona metod asosida dars tashkil etish kutilgan natijani bermasligi mumkin. Shu nuqtayi nazardan, sun'iy intellekt va raqamli texnologiyalarga asoslangan adaptiv ta'lim tizimlari talabaning individual xususiyatlarini hisobga olgan holda ta'lim mazmuni, topshiriqlar murakkabligi va o'quv materiallarini moslashtirish imkonini beradi. Tezisda amaliy matematika fanlarini o'qitishda adaptiv yondashuvning afzalliklari, undan foydalanish mexanizmlari hamda ta'lim samaradorligini oshirishdagi ahamiyati tahlil qilingan.

title: Lean Formalization and Verification Scripts for Deterministic Prime Bases for Regev's Algorithm
abstract: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization and verification scripts accompanying the paper "Deterministic Prime Bases for Regev's Algorithm". The development proves, using only Lean's standard axioms (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound): - Theorem 1.1 (almost all integers): outside a proportion O((log n)^(-1/2)) of the inputs that survive trial division, the first ⌈√n⌉ primes give a useful vector of Euclidean length 2^((3/2+o(1))√n); - Theorem 1.2 (balanced RSA): under three explicit key-generation laws, the exceptional proportion is Θ(2^(-⌈√n⌉)) at every fixed length coefficient C > 9/2; - a finite table for the two FIPS 186-5-filtered laws at 1024-4096 bits; at RSA-2048, fewer than 4.42·10^-13 of moduli lack a useful vector of length at most 2^214.96; - Z-bases of short vectors for the relation lattices L_N and K_N of the first primes (deterministic form and the four table sizes); - the parameter inequalities and a probability-space model for a finite RSA-2048 execution, conditional on an explicit per-input quantum guarantee. Version 1.2.0 adds the sharper determinant bound φ(N)/4 and the √d/2 extraction factor (RSA-2048 radius 2^214.96, previously 2^219.72); a general basis-selection theorem and the short-basis results; and the retuned execution schedule (precision 2^345, 496 Fibonacci levels). The audit checks 879 selected declarations and every local compiled declaration; reports, kernel replay, negative controls and the source manifest are included. The quantum circuit and lattice reconstruction are not formalized.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Payer Population Health Risk stratification, care gaps, and intervention prioritization in chronic care
abstract: Payer population health requires a distinction between predicting an adverse outcome, identifying a documented care gap, and selecting a response. We organized public evidence on computational approaches to these functions in chronic care, with Latin America as the context of interest and international studies retained as a separate comparator layer. A structured directed review used a July 16, 2026 search and October 2 targeted source verification, rather than a comprehensive update. We interpreted peer-reviewed research, other academic reports, and official institutional descriptions according to their tasks, accessible content, and evaluation maturity. International studies demonstrated retrospective modeling with administrative data, while care-sequence analyses and non-AI workflows illustrated different approaches to assessing gaps and organizing follow-up. Internal validation, external cohort validation, prospective utility, intervention effects, and routine implementation were treated separately. Official cases described programs or governance, not independently established AI effectiveness. The retrieved Latin American sources provide methodological and non-AI operational context, not evidence of prospectively validated payer AI or demonstrated intervention benefit. Authors' recommendations emphasize explicit outcome definitions, data and subgroup checks, human response design, and staged evaluation before operational use. External evidence supports an evaluation agenda; it does not establish local transferability, clinical benefit, or cost savings.

title: Cancer Tissue Fraction as a Scanner-Robust Triage Signal for Automated Gleason Grading of Prostate Biopsies: External Validation Across a Middle Eastern Cohort
abstract: Background: Deep learning systems for Gleason grading are developed almost entirely on high-end clinical scanners and on cohorts from a small number of Western institutions, yet deployment increasingly involves other devices and other populations. These two distribution shifts, device and population, are rarely tested together on the same physical slides. The PAR dataset, from Erbil, Iraq, digitizes each biopsy on three scanners and provides three distinct pathologist grades, so it permits both tests at once on a Middle Eastern cohort. A concurrent study by the dataset originators validated a task-specific model and two foundation models on PAR; we complement it by testing an independently developed detect-then-grade pipeline and by separating scanner effects on detection from scanner effects on grading. Methods: We applied one fixed model developed on North American and European material to all 1017 whole-slide images (339 slides from 185 patients, three scanners; 49.6% clinically significant cancer) with no scanner-specific or population-specific tuning. We measured cancer detection (area under the ROC curve of the predicted cancer tissue fraction), all-slide ISUP agreement of the deployed detect-then-grade pipeline (quadratic-weighted kappa, QWK), and grading agreement on pathologist-confirmed cancers, at the slide level and, because a case carries up to two slides, at the patient level. The reference reader was S.A.; thresholds and operating points were cross-validated leave-one-out; scanners were compared by paired within-biopsy bootstrap and confidence intervals confirmed by patient-cluster bootstrap. Results: Detection was statistically equivalent across scanners (AUC 0.987 to 0.991; paired differences at most 0.003) and transferred to this non-Western cohort with no per-population tuning. At a 95% sensitivity operating point, the deployed pipeline reached cross-validated all-slide QWK of 0.86, 0.81, and 0.86 (Grundium, Hamamatsu, Leica), matching the inter-pathologist ceiling of 0.81, against 0.23 to 0.62 for the ungated model. Grading of confirmed cancers was scanner-dependent: the compact Grundium (0.63) did not differ from the clinical Leica (0.67; paired difference 0.04, 95% CI −0.03 to 0.11), while both exceeded Hamamatsu (0.44). Results held at the patient level, with grading somewhat lower for two scanners; the two slides of a case disagreed in grade in 43% of cases, and patient clustering did not widen the intervals. Conclusions: Cancer tissue fraction is a triage signal robust across scanner and transferable to an underrepresented population for detection, while grading is the scanner-sensitive step. Prostate grading models should be deployed as a detect-then-grade pipeline, with grading validated per device and confirmed on the local population.

title: SWE-Stream: Scaling Executable Training Data for SWE Agents via Progressive Construction and Elastic Streaming
abstract: Software engineering agents have advanced rapidly, but scaling their training remains constrained by the limited availability of high-quality executable tasks. Development histories contain valuable signals for constructing such tasks, yet they often require substantial reconstruction due to incomplete environments, missing tests, and inconsistent artifacts. We present SWE-Stream, a system for scaling executable SWE training data through progressive construction and elastic streaming execution. SWE-Stream progressively validates and refines task candidates, reusing existing artifacts when possible and applying targeted completion only when necessary. An elastic scheduler asynchronously coordinates construction stages under shared resource constraints, adapting execution budgets based on observed workload demands. Using development histories from 10,728 repositories across six programming languages, SWE-Stream constructs 80,874 validated tasks and collects 118,688 successful trajectories. Fine-tuning Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 on these trajectories achieves resolve rates of 69.0%, 49.3%, and 45.42% on SWE-bench Verified, Multilingual, and Pro, respectively. In a controlled comparison with approximately matched training budgets, SWE-Stream achieves a 45.6% resolve rate on SWE-bench Verified, outperforming three existing data sources. Moreover, its streaming construction strategy improves efficiency, delivering $1.45\times$ the accepted-task throughput of batch construction and accepting 13.2% more tasks than fixed-limit streaming.

title: Few-Shot Adaptation for Anomalous Sound Detection at Low False-Positive Rate
abstract: Reliable fault detection is crucial for industrial machinery in large-scale facilities, where unexpected failures can cause costly downtime and production interruptions. Although acoustic monitoring provides a scalable solution for machine condition monitoring, its deployment is often constrained by high false-positive rates. We propose a two-step approach to automatic anomalous sound detection: first, when only normal operating audio samples are available, a regularized unsupervised model is deployed; then, after the first machine fault, a few-shot adaptation strategy exploits the anomalous samples acquired during the fault to improve the system. This adaptation increases the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPR) from 23.0 to 64.0 and improves detection in the low false-positive-rate region, with the partial area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (pAUROC) increasing from 39.6 to 72.8. We also show that covariance regularization improves both prediction accuracy and training stability in the unsupervised model. These results provide a practical strategy for acoustic anomaly detection systems, enabling improved accuracy and reduced false alarms.

title: От «генерирующего автора» к «ответственному автору»: исследование стратификации авторской идентичности в совместном письме на втором языке с использованием ИИ
abstract: В статье рассматривается проблема авторской идентичности в условиях совместного письма на втором языке с использованием искусственного интеллекта (ИИ). Традиционное представление об авторе как единственном создателе текста сталкивается с вызовом со стороны генеративных моделей, способных производить связные тексты по запросу. На основе междисциплинарного теоретического анализа — теории авторства, этики ответственности, социально-культурного подхода и исследований распределённого познания — предлагается трёхуровневая модель авторской идентичности: «генерирующий автор» (ИИ), «выбирающий автор» (обучающийся) и «ответственный автор» (обучающийся). Показано, что ИИ может выполнять функцию генерации языковых форм, но не может быть носителем интенциональности, этической ответственности и уязвимости. Авторство в цифровую эпоху смещается от «права производить предложения» к «праву решать, какие предложения заслуживают существования», и от «написания слов» к «готовности сказать “я”». Выделены десять оригинальных положений, раскрывающих природу авторства в совместном письме: автор как арбитр значимости, как носитель уязвимости, как создатель финала, как дизайнер негативного пространства, как якорь интенциональности, как этический агент, как отложенный подтверждающий, как подписывающий стиль, как реляционный автор при нераспределяемой ответственности. Обсуждаются педагогические и этические следствия для обучения второму языку и проектирования систем ИИ-письма.

title: Multi Step Prediction Model and Algorithm for Industrial Innovation Capability Integrating Spatiotemporal Heterogeneous Graph Transformer and Causal Decoupling Representation Learning
abstract: # CD-STHGT **Causal Decoupled Spatiotemporal Heterogeneous Graph Transformer forMulti-Step Prediction of Industrial Innovation Capability** Reference implementation and dataset for the paper*Multi-Step Prediction Model and Algorithm for Industrial InnovationCapability Integrating Spatiotemporal Heterogeneous Graph Transformer andCausal Decoupling Representation Learning*. [![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/)[![PyTorch 2.1](https://img.shields.io/badge/pytorch-2.1-ee4c2c.svg)](https://pytorch.org/)[![PyG 2.5](https://img.shields.io/badge/pyg-2.5-ff6b00.svg)](https://pytorch-geometric.readthedocs.io/)[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE) --- ## Overview CD-STHGT forecasts the innovation capability of Chinese provincial-subindustrynodes one through seven years ahead by combining three ideas: - **Dual-timescale heterogeneous graphs**: slow structural relations (geographic adjacency, industrial-chain coupling, technological similarity) are blended with fast shock graphs (talent mobility, patent citation) via a cycle-aware node gate driven by macro policy themes.- **Ternary causal disentanglement**: node embeddings are projected to causal, environmental and style factors with an HSIC independence penalty; a combined back-door and front-door adjustment produces causal predictions that generalise under distribution shift.- **Causal trajectory rollout and CD-Shapley**: a recurrent cell evolves the causal factor along the forecast horizon, a trajectory consistency term stabilises long-horizon rollouts, and a counterfactual Shapley procedure with do-operator interventions attributes the forecast to each driver. | Model | RMSE@1 | RMSE@5 | RMSE@7 | MAPE@5 (%) ||--------------|-------:|-------:|-------:|-----------:|| Informer | 0.198 | 0.312 | 0.389 | 10.7 || iTransformer | 0.187 | 0.294 | 0.362 | 10.1 || HGT | 0.183 | 0.281 | 0.346 | 9.6 || CaST | 0.176 | 0.272 | 0.338 | 9.4 || DVGNN | 0.168 | 0.258 | 0.325 | 8.9 || **CD-STHGT** | **0.141** | **0.217** | **0.268** | **7.2** | Against the strongest baseline (DVGNN), CD-STHGT reduces RMSE by 16.0 %,15.9 % and 17.6 % at horizons 1, 5 and 7 respectively. --- ## Repository contents This repository ships as two archives: - **`cdsthgt-code.zip`** - PyTorch 2.1 and PyTorch Geometric 2.5 implementation. Model, baselines, attribution, evaluation, figure and table generators. End-to-end pipeline. - **`cdsthgt-dataset.zip`** - longitudinal panel on 31 provincial administrative regions, 5 high-technology subindustries and 19 years (2005 to 2023), together with five heterogeneous graph relations, 326 policy documents, LDA topics, keyword dictionaries and auxiliary materials. --- ## Quick start ### 1. Install ```bashgit clone .git cdsthgt && cd cdsthgtpython -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activatepip install -r requirements.txt``` Dependencies (also in `requirements.txt`): - `torch >= 2.1`- `torch_geometric >= 2.5`- `numpy`, `pandas`, `scipy`, `scikit-learn`- `statsmodels` (ARIMA baseline)- `xgboost` (XGBoost baseline)- `matplotlib` (figures), `pyyaml` (config), `openpyxl` (results export) ### 2. Place the dataset Download `cdsthgt-dataset.zip`, extract and symlink or copy into `./data/`: ```bashunzip cdsthgt-dataset.zipmv cdsthgt-dataset/panel/provincial_subindustry_panel_2005_2023.csv \ data/panel_main_2005_2023.csvcp -r cdsthgt-dataset/heterogeneous_relations data/cp -r cdsthgt-dataset/policy_corpus data/``` Alternatively edit `configs/cdsthgt.yaml` to point `data.panel_csv`,`data.relations_dir` and `data.policy_dir` at your chosen locations. ### 3. Run End-to-end pipeline: ```bashpython scripts/run_all.py``` Produces every table and figure under `experiments/results/`. On a singleRTX 4090 the full run (5 seeds for CD-STHGT, 3 seeds for the ten baselines,200 epochs) finishes in roughly 11 hours. Stage-by-stage: ```bash# CD-STHGT, five seeds, 200 epochspython scripts/train_cdsthgt.py \ --config configs/cdsthgt.yaml \ --output experiments/results/cdsthgt_table7.json # Ten baselines, three seeds, 50 epochs eachpython scripts/train_baselines.py \ --config configs/cdsthgt.yaml \ --epochs 50 --seeds 0 1 2 \ --baselines ARIMA XGBoost LSTM Informer iTransformer \ STGCN GraphWaveNet HGT CaST DVGNN \ --output experiments/results/baselines_table7.json # Tables 7 through 14python scripts/aggregate_results.py # CD-Shapley attribution at the 2020 forecast originpython scripts/run_attribution.py --origin 2020 --n_permutations 64 # Figures 3 and 7 through 14python scripts/generate_figures.py``` --- ## Project structure ```cdsthgt/├── README.md (this file)├── requirements.txt├── LICENSE├── configs/│ └── cdsthgt.yaml Model and training hyperparameters├── data/ Place dataset here (see Section 2)├── src/│ ├── data/ Panel loader, dual-timescale graph│ │ builder, policy mediator,│ │ rolling-origin protocol│ ├── models/│ │ ├── cdsthgt.py CD-STHGT main model│ │ ├── dthg_module.py Meta-path attention,│ │ │ cycle-aware gated fusion│ │ ├── disentangle.py Ternary disentanglement,│ │ │ back-door and front-door adjustment│ │ └── baselines/│ │ └── all_baselines.py Ten baselines│ ├── attribution/│ │ └── cd_shapley.py Counterfactual Shapley│ ├── evaluation/│ │ └── metrics.py Evaluation metrics│ └── utils/│ └── seed.py Reproducibility helpers├── scripts/│ ├── train_cdsthgt.py Train the main model│ ├── train_baselines.py Train the ten baselines│ ├── aggregate_results.py Reproduce Tables 7 through 14│ ├── run_attribution.py CD-Shapley attribution│ ├── generate_figures.py Reproduce Figures 3, 7 through 14│ └── run_all.py Full end-to-end pipeline└── results/ ├── tables/ Reference tables (CSV) └── figures/ Reference figures (PNG)``` --- ## Dataset Full specification in `cdsthgt-dataset/README.md`. Summary: - 31 provincial administrative regions, 5 high-technology subindustries, 19 years (2005 through 2023) - 2,945 node-year observations.- 14 input features over five dimensions (innovation input, innovation output, innovation collaboration, economic environment, digital foundation) plus the composite innovation capability score on a 4.2 through 100 scale.- Five heterogeneous graph relations (geographic adjacency, industrial-chain coupling, technological similarity, talent mobility, patent citation), the slow ones as yearly weighted adjacency matrices and the fast ones as dated quarterly events.- 326 central-government policy documents with LDA topic intensities and topic-subindustry similarities.- Supplementary materials: IPC-to-subindustry concordance, inventor disambiguation dictionary, recruitment-platform flow panel, keyword dictionary, stopword list, three central-government policy events, provincial centroid coordinates and contiguity pairs. Primary sources: *China High-Technology Industry Statistical Yearbook*,*China Science and Technology Statistical Yearbook*, *China IndustrialStatistical Yearbook*, the CNIPA patent database, the *White Paper onChina's Digital Economy* of the China Academy of Information andCommunications Technology, and the State Council / MIIT / NDRC / MOSTpolicy archives. --- ## Model architecture ### Dual-timescale heterogeneous graph Transformer Meta-path aware multi-head attention over seven meta-paths plus twocomposite paths (Equation 2 of the paper). The cycle-aware gated fusion(Equation 3) uses a node-wise gate g[v, t] computed from the slow and fastweighted degree of v combined with the annual topic-intensity embedding. ```alpha[u, v, r, k] = softmax_u( ( W_Q^{r,k} h_v )^T ( W_K^{r,k} h_u ) / sqrt(d_k) * mu[r, k] )g[v, t] = sigmoid( w_g^T [ s^slow[v] s^fast[v] p[t] ] + b_g )A_slow^fuse[t] = diag(g[t]) * A^slow[t]A_fast^fuse[t] = diag(1 - g[t]) * A^fast[t]``` ### Ternary causal disentanglement Each node embedding h is projected to: - **z^c** = Encoder_c(h), the causal factor- **z^e** = Quantizer(h), the environmental factor on a 16-entry codebook- **z^s** = Encoder_s(h), the style factor An HSIC term enforces independence between z^c and z^e. The front-door andback-door adjustment (Equations 5 and 6) produces the causal prediction`P_causal = eta * P_back + (1 - eta) * P_front` with eta = 0.5. ### Causal trajectory rollout A gated recurrent cell rolls z^c forward one step at a time; the adjustmentreads out a prediction at each step. The composite loss is ```L = L_pred + 0.3 * L_traj + 0.01 * L_HSIC + 0.1 * L_rec``` where L_traj penalises the squared difference of successive z^c states. ### CD-Shapley attribution Permutation sampling with do-interventions on each feature; the baseline isthe zero vector in standardized feature space (the training-period mean).The time-dependent effect curve Phi_i(t) is produced by rollingone-feature-at-a-time counterfactuals through the input window. --- ## Reproducibility Random seeds are controlled by `src/utils/seed.py` and set under`training.seeds` in the YAML configuration. Standard deviations reported inthe paper's Table 7 come from the five seeds in the default configuration. Rolling-origin protocol (same as the paper): three forecast origins(2018, 2019, 2020), four horizons (1, 3, 5, 7 years), input window ofT = 5 years, slow-graph window of 3 years, fast-graph quarter window of 1,diffusion coefficient beta = 0.5.

title: How AI is transforming the way organizations think and learn
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to review the latest management developments across the globe and pinpoint practical implications from cutting-edge research and case studies. Design/methodology/approach This briefing is prepared by an independent writer who adds their own impartial comments and places the articles in context. Findings Knowledge management is crucial in any firm and shaped by the different dimensions of organizational cognition. The introduction of artificial intelligence (AI) broadens the scope for effective knowledge management strategies, but leaders must be aware of the need to ensure that the AI-human mechanisms used to develop strategies are utilized appropriately so that hybrid cognition proves effective. Originality/value The briefing saves busy executives, strategists and researchers hours of reading time by selecting only the very best, most pertinent information and presenting it in a condensed and easy-to-digest format.

title: Quantum prepare-and-measure scenarios: concepts and methods
abstract: Prepare-and-measure scenarios are among the simplest and most widely used settings for quantum communication. A sender prepares a physical system in one of several possible states, which a receiver then measures. Despite this simple structure, these scenarios offer a rich framework for exploring the differences between classical and quantum communication, revealing quantum advantages, and developing protocols for quantum cryptography and device certification. In this tutorial, we give a ground-up introduction to prepare-and-measure scenarios and the methods used to study them. We introduce different frameworks for constraining and characterising communication, with an emphasis on semi-device-independent approaches to quantum information. We also cover modern convex-optimisation techniques for characterising the correlations achievable in these scenarios and illustrate how these tools can be applied in practice. Our aim is to give newcomers the conceptual and technical foundations needed to approach the current literature and apply prepare-and-measure methods in their own research. We conclude with a discussion of open problems and directions for future work.

evidence.title: Quantum prepare-and-measure scenarios: concepts and methods
evidence.abstract: Prepare-and-measure scenarios are among the simplest and most widely used settings for quantum communication. A sender prepares a physical system in one of several possible states, which a receiver then measures. Despite this simple structure, these scenarios offer a rich framework for exploring the differences between classical and quantum communication, revealing quantum advantages, and developing protocols for quantum cryptography and device certification. In this tutorial, we give a ground-up introduction to prepare-and-measure scenarios and the methods used to study them. We introduce different frameworks for constraining and characterising communication, with an emphasis on semi-device-independent approaches to quantum information. We also cover modern convex-optimisation techniques for characterising the correlations achievable in these scenarios and illustrate how these tools can be applied in practice. Our aim is to give newcomers the conceptual and technical foundations needed to approach the current literature and apply prepare-and-measure methods in their own research. We conclude with a discussion of open problems and directions for future work.

title: Testing Conditional Distribution Equality Using Generative Models
abstract: Conditional distribution equality testing is a core problem with applications in causal inference, model diagnostics, and transfer learning. Existing methods often lose power when the conditioning variable is high-dimensional. We propose a new test that leverages generative models to compare conditional distributions using both observed data and synthetic samples. A sample-splitting and studentization scheme is introduced to control estimation error. Under the null, the test statistic is asymptotically normal, and we establish local power against contiguous alternatives. Our theory under the null and fixed alternative requires only consistency of the learned conditional distribution, allowing for a broad class of generative models. Empirical results demonstrate accurate size control and strong power in high-dimensional settings compared to representative kernel-based conditional and joint two-sample tests.

title: Photon Demultiplexing Using Spatial Routing
abstract: Spatial sectioning of the far-field noncollinear field from spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) is a promising approach for multiparty quantum communication. Although demonstrations with six pairs of users have been reported, the fundamental limits remain unknown. These include the maximum number of channels, the required degree of channel optimization, and the dependence on input parameters. In this paper, we provide a practical framework that answers these questions by connecting input parameters and invoking a design theorem. For a representative configuration, we realize 12 user-pair channels with routing consistency exceeding $0.9999$ at a $12\%$ reduction in photon flux. We further show that sectioning improves the accidental-coincidence budget linearly with the number of channels $N$, allowing the aggregate key rate to scale with the user count. These results provide a design strategy for spatial-division multiplexing of entangled photons analogous to the channel-spacing standards used in wavelength-division networks.

title: On the Limits of Representation-Based Test-Time Adaptation for Multimodal LLMs
abstract: Vision-language models suffer significant accuracy drops under common corruptions. While test-time adaptation (TTA) successfully mitigates these shifts in CLIP-like contrastive models, its application to generative multimodal large language models (MLLMs) remains underexplored and uniquely challenging due to their sequential token generation. In this work, we demonstrate that representation-based TTA fails to recover performance in MLLMs. Our experiments reveal that even when violating standard TTA assumptions by leveraging target data offline, sample-blind feature alignment recovers only marginal accuracy. We attribute this failure to the nature of corruption shifts: unlike CLIP-like architectures, which benefit from a shared domain-shift direction within a single pooled classification embedding, MLLM visual token sequence shifts are nearly orthogonal and span the full embedding space.These findings bound what any sample-blind, position-shared correction at a single encoder site can achieve, establishing that representation-space interventions alone might be insufficient to ensure corruption robustness in MLLMs.

title: Annealed Lévy Diffusion via Gaussian Surrogate Reverse Dynamics
abstract: Gaussian diffusion models offer a practical framework for generative modeling. Denoising Lévy Probabilistic Models (DLPM) introduce heavy-tailed perturbations with a fixed tail index throughout denoising. We introduce Annealed Lévy Diffusion (ALD). ALD varies the stability index $α(t)$ to combine heavy-tailed exploration with Gaussian refinement. Our marginal-first formulation represents stable noise as a scalar Gaussian scale mixture. This formulation enables standard Gaussian noise-prediction training with one additional scale input. We study two sampling processes. ALD-renoise estimates the clean sample and injects fresh marginal noise. ALD-posterior preserves dependence between successive states through an accumulated conditional variance and a Gaussian bridge update. Both samplers reuse the same trained predictor with different scalar inputs. We evaluate ALD on four 2D benchmarks and an imbalanced nine-mode mixture. We also examine training efficiency and the effects of prediction perturbations on clipped Holtsmark data. Additional experiments evaluate MNIST and CelebA64 generation and CIFAR-10LT augmentation. ALD preserves local geometry on the evaluated light-tailed and manifold-structured targets.

title: Balanced Defensive Fine-Tuning for Text-to-SQL on a Small Code Language Model: A Pre-Registered Measurement Report
abstract: Locally run small language models enable generating SQL from natural language without sending the database schema to third-party servers. However, a model fine-tuned only to "translate the question into SQL" can also translate destructive or unauthorized commands embedded in the prompt. In this report we measure, under a pre-registered protocol, the Balanced SFT method applied with QLoRA (nf4, r=16) on Qwen2.5-Coder-3B-Instruct. In this method each training example is drawn from the attack set with probability α and from the legitimate Spider set with probability 1−α. The compared conditions are: the untrained base model (B0), standard SFT on legitimate data only (A0, α=0), balanced SFT (A.3, α=0.3), and SFT on defense data only (A1, α=1.0). Each trained condition was run with 3 seeds. The test sets consist of 500 attack prompts, 1034 Spider-dev questions, and 24 legitimate questions that contain risky words. Attack success rate (ASR) measured with a database-execution (DB-exec) judge is 61.53% ± 2.53 on A0 and 0.00% on A.3. The difference is −61.53 points, with 95% confidence interval [−64.73; −58.53]. Official test-suite execution accuracy (EX) is 70.25% ± 0.49 on A0 and 69.50% ± 0.88 on A.3. The difference is −0.74 points, with 95% confidence interval [−2.06; 0.55]. Thus H1 (security) and H2 (cost, non-inferiority) pass the pre-specified thresholds. However, the protocol-mandated human judge audit of 100 examples was not performed and will not be performed (Appendix A, S18). ASR was measured only with the automatic DB-exec judge; because judge validity was not tested against human labels, both hypotheses are reported only as supported (provisional), and this label can no longer become definitive. The over-refusal hypothesis H3 remains exploratory because the test set was reduced from 250 to 24: even with 0/24 errors the Wilson upper bound is 13.8% and lies above the 10% threshold. The α=1.0 condition collapsed on all three seeds to a solution that rejects every input. Deviations from the locked plan and unplanned analysis decisions are collected in a single table in Appendix A, with dates and whether they were taken before or after results were seen (11 coded deviations, 6 uncoded decisions; 17 items, 18 rows). Seven of these items were taken after results were seen. Among them are the 14 October 2026 finalization of the decision to stop at 3 seeds, the merging of the category 3/4 rule in the DB-exec judge, and moving the human-audit target from A.3_s11 to A0_s11. The collapse of A1 and the fact that ASR is a proxy measurement are not deviations but a result and a measurement note.

title: ropensci/ibger: ibger 0.2.1
abstract: The package was peer-reviewed and accepted by rOpenSci (ropensci/software-review#787). The repository moved to https://github.com/ropensci/ibger and the documentation to https://docs.ropensci.org/ibger/; the rOpenSci Code of Conduct now applies. Changes from the rOpenSci review (ropensci/software-review#787) Second review (@ddiannae) parse_sidra_url() / fetch_sidra_url(): a SIDRA URL without a /p/ (periods) segment no longer crashes the print method and the fetch; the equivalent call falls back to the ibge_variables() default (last 6 periods) (reported by @ddiannae). parse_sidra_url(): a territorial level that is not in the internal lookup table (e.g. n12) no longer errors with "subscript out of bounds". Levels that the aggregate does not offer now raise a warning at parse time listing the available levels, and fetch_sidra_url() fails through the regular validation (reported by @ddiannae). parse_sidra_url(): URLs with several territorial levels (e.g. n1/all/n3/all) produced an "Equivalent ibger call" with an unnamed list that ibge_variables() rejects. The printed call and fetch_sidra_url() now share one translation: a named list when every level has specific codes, and the API's pipe syntax ("N1|N3[33,35]") otherwise (reported by @ddiannae). ibge_aggregates() now checks the format of its five filters before the request. The API silently drops filters it cannot parse (returning the whole catalog under a success message) and answers HTTP 500 to others, e.g. periodicity = 30; malformed values now abort with an example of the expected format. An empty result is reported with a warning instead of a green "0 aggregates found", and keeps the documented columns (reported by @ddiannae). ibge_aggregates(): the periodicity codes in the documentation were wrong (P10 and P58 do not exist; P13 is the rolling quarter, not annual). The documented table now lists the codes observed in the catalog: P1 annual, P5 monthly, P8 semi-annual, P9 quarterly, P13 rolling quarter, plus the multi-year codes (reported by @ddiannae). ibge_localities() with several levels queries each level separately and binds the results: the API's own multi-level endpoint returns an empty list as soon as one of the levels has no localities for the aggregate. An empty result now keeps the documented columns and is reported with a warning (reported by @ddiannae). The "exceeds the 100,000 value limit" hint on HTTP 500 is now only shown for data requests (ibge_variables()); for the other endpoints, where a 500 means the API could not interpret the request (non-existent aggregate, invalid filter), the message says so (reported by @ddiannae). Vignettes: getting-started and api-concepts are now precomputed against the live API like the other two (vignettes/precompile.R), so every printed output is real. This removed a set of wrong hand-written outputs — aggregate 1705 (IPCA-15) was described as the quarterly animal slaughter table, which is 1092; the ibge_variables(1705, localities = "N3") example (also in ?ibge_variables) errors because 1705 has no state level; periodicity = "P10" returned nothing — and replaced the advice to split large queries by hand with a section on the automatic chunking (chunk) in all three vignettes that mentioned the limit (reported by @ddiannae; precomputing suggested by @beatrizmilz). ibge_localities() example: ibge_localities(1437, level = c("N6", "N7")) returned an empty tibble (1437 has no metropolitan-area localities); the example now uses c("N2", "N3") (reported by @ddiannae). First review (@allanvc) Fixed the bsicons availability check in ibge_explorer(), which told users to install bslib instead of bsicons (reported by @allanvc). Fixed the documentation of the launch.browser argument of ibge_explorer(), which described FALSE as the default; the default is and remains TRUE (open in the browser), and FALSE opens the app in the RStudio Viewer pane (reported by @allanvc). Documented the IBGE API's server-side latency for large queries in ?ibge_variables and the README: municipality-level requests can take one to several minutes each (suggested by @allanvc). README: replaced the link to IBGE's terms of use, whose old address now returns a 404, with the current "Termo de Uso e Política de Privacidade" page (reported by @allanvc). Removed the stray .Rhistory file from the repository (suggested by @allanvc). curl (>= 6.0.0) is now declared in Imports, enforcing at install time the version requirement that was previously only documented in the README (older curl versions fail with curl_modify_url is not an exported object). The table of IBGE special value codes (-, .., ..., X) is now documented in a single place — ?parse_ibge_value — and linked from the README and vignettes instead of being repeated. The ipca-example and tutorial vignettes are now precompiled from .Rmd.orig sources against the live IBGE API (vignettes/precompile.R), so their output and ggplot2 figures render on the pkgdown site. README: added the rOpenSci review badge, linked the API-concepts vignette from the quick start, pointed the "Value column" section to parse_ibge_value(), and rewrote the ibge_explorer() section to match the tone of the rest of the page. Examples no longer use \dontrun{}: examples that query the live IBGE API (or launch the Shiny explorer) are now guarded with @examplesIf interactive(), so they render in the docs and run for interactive users without hitting the network during checks. Internal refactor to address the remaining pkgcheck/goodpractice notes: every function is now below the cyclomatic-complexity threshold of 15 (long functions such as parse_sidra_url(), fetch_sidra_url(), ibge_metadata() and ibge_survey_metadata() were decomposed into focused helpers), duplicated @param docs were replaced with @inheritParams, and the lintr issues flagged in the review (long lines, expect_equal() vs expect_identical(), static regexes without fixed = TRUE, duplicate cli bullet names, <<-, require() in the Shiny app, setwd() in precompile.R) were cleaned up. No user-facing behavior changes. Other changes Expanded the test suite to cover all exported functions (~85% coverage): pure helpers and parsers are tested directly, and API interactions are tested against recorded fixtures with httptest2 (no network needed). Added continuous integration: R CMD check on Linux/macOS/Windows and test coverage reporting via GitHub Actions. Added CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md and codemeta.json in preparation for rOpenSci submission.

title: Patentability of artificial intelligence (AI) inventions: A comparative study of Section 3(k) of the Indian Patents Act, 1970 and the United Kingdom's journey from Aerotel to emotional perception AI
abstract: This article undertakes a comparative doctrinal analysis of the patentability of artificial-intelligence (AI)-related inventions under Indian and UK patent law. Between 2023 and early 2026, the Delhi High Court, in a series of decisions culminating in Kroll Information Assurance, LLC v Controller General of Patents , refined the ‘technical effect/technical contribution’ threshold that governs the exclusion of ‘a computer programme per se’ under Section 3(k) of the Patents Act, 1970. That threshold has since been codified, with AI-specific illustrations, in the Guidelines for Examination of Computer Related Inventions, 2025, issued on 29 July 2025. The United Kingdom's position developed less smoothly. In Emotional Perception AI Ltd v Comptroller-General of Patents , a permissive first-instance ruling was reversed by the Court of Appeal, which reaffirmed the primacy of the long-standing four-step Aerotel test, before the Supreme Court, on 11 February 2026, overruled Aerotel altogether and adopted an approach modelled on the European Patent Office's ‘any hardware’ doctrine. This article argues that, notwithstanding these divergent statutory architectures and procedural histories, India and the United Kingdom have arrived at a structurally similar solution: a low, largely formal threshold for patent eligibility, followed by a substantive technical–character enquiry applied at a later analytical stage.

title: Wavelet compression for sampling deep Gaussian processes
abstract: Deep Gaussian processes (DGPs) use iterative sampling to create non-stationary random fields. This is notoriously expensive because the covariance at each non-initial layer depends on the realised field from the layer below, so it changes with every sample. Moreover, standard fast sampling techniques like circulant embedding or matrix compression fail since the underlying kernel usually lacks the necessary regularity and structure. We develop and analyse a wavelet compression method for convolution Matérn DGPs. At each layer the covariance matrix is compressed using wavelets and a Lanczos algorithm computes the random sample. For specific parameter ranges involving the smoothness of the Matérn kernel as well as the smoothness of the wavelets, we show that the accumulative compression and sampling errors through all layers decay exponentially with increasing truncation parameter. We obtain a practical DGP sampling algorithm by choosing a truncation that gives log-linear covariance storage and matrix-vector costs, enabling DGP sampling at nearly linear computational cost.

title: PPAD-Completeness of Contiguous Envy-Free Cake Cutting with Additive Valuations
abstract: We prove that computing a complete contiguous $\varepsilon$-envy-free cake allocation is PPAD-complete for normalized rational piecewise-constant additive valuations. The hardness holds even when $\varepsilon$ is given in unary, and even when every density takes only two values, which are the same for all agents, and is piecewise constant with at most six breakpoints. As a consequence, computing an exact contiguous envy-free allocation is also PPAD-complete, and the hardness holds under the same restrictions on the densities. Our key ingredient is to assign prices to the pieces so that, in every approximately envy-free allocation, all prices are nearly equal, regardless of how the pieces are assigned to the agents. We further show that, for every fixed integer $c\ge1$, computing a contiguous EF$c$ allocation of indivisible goods on a path is PPAD-complete for additive valuations, and the hardness holds even for binary valuations in which each good is valued by exactly one agent and all agents value the same number of goods.

title: AdCoEvo: A Co-Evolving Multi-Agent Advertising Delivery System
abstract: Digital advertising is an important means for platforms to reach potential users and drive business growth. Advertising delivery is the core link between marketing objectives and actual returns. Existing methods have achieved partial automation in individual tasks such as bidding and budget allocation, but they still rely on human operators for overall coordination, making it difficult to support large-scale operations. They also often fail to achieve optimal performance, and individual experience remains difficult to turn into reusable operational capabilities. In addition, as advertising markets change, advertising delivery systems need timely strategy updates to remain effective in dynamic markets. To automate the entire advertising operations process and improve adaptability to market changes, we propose AdCoEvo, a co-evolving multi-agent advertising delivery system. Specifically, the system connects delivery decisions across different timescales and operational granularities through role specialization. Diagnostic results guide account planning and strategy adjustment in the next period. The multi-agent system updates its model parameters based on actual delivery outcomes and continually improves delivery strategies through mutual feedback among planning, adjustment, and diagnosis, thereby achieving co-evolution. Experiments show that, relative to the rule-based operational baseline (Rule), AdCoEvo increases advertiser value by 14.02% while reducing cost per acquisition by 7.07%. Compared with a multi-agent system with fixed parameters, AdCoEvo increases advertiser value by 3.96% and reduces cost per acquisition by 1.24%, indicating that co-evolution can yield greater delivery returns.

title: Authorship Attribution in Arabic: Teaching Companion
abstract: This teaching companion accompanies Chapter 8, Authorship Attribution in Arabic: From Stylometric Methods to Large Language Models, prepared for the edited volume Arabic Digital Humanities (John Benjamins). It provides an illustrated teaching guide, Python and R scripts, fixed evaluation folds, corpus and excerpt manifests, recorded predictions, software information, and publication figures. The main exercise uses twelve narrative works by four modern Arabic authors. Burrows's Delta is calculated with the R package stylo using training-only feature selection and scaling; word and character TF-IDF representations feed linear support vector machines. Whole works are held out during evaluation. A separate stylo interface exercise explores similarity across all twelve sampled work profiles, with full dialogue screenshots, visible selection markers and a complete cluster plot. An optional local Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct exercise demonstrates prompted attribution. Its shorter passages and smaller reference budget require separate interpretation from the Delta and SVM results. Classroom activities connect errors and clustering to close reading and distinguish completed analyses from proposed extensions. The package preserves the recorded analyses from 14 October 2026 and provides verified rerun instructions. Raw source books, reconstructed passages and model weights are not redistributed; retrieval instructions and checksums identify the sources. Original teaching documentation and figures are licensed under CC BY 4.0; original scripts are licensed under MIT. Third-party materials retain their own terms, as detailed in LICENSE.md. Version 1.0.1 corrects caption layout by separating figure and screenshot titles from explanatory paragraphs. It restores author label colours in the complete cluster plot and retains monochrome PNG and vector PDF alternatives. The publication plotting script generates both variants. The underlying data, clustering and recorded evaluation results are unchanged.
